process-scheduled-payouts.why: PROVEN 2026-09-22T16:40:58Z, money actually moved: Stripe transfer tr_3UILijKp2H4b7tEC1WjXCD25, $22.00, destination acct_1UCU7J4HVr518r7O, destination_payment py_1UIWkX4HVr518r7OLqZDhsQv status=succeeded — the helper's connected account went $0 -> $22.00 pending. Ledger row initiated_by='system' (not admin), amount_cents=2200, platform_fee_cents=300; job -> released. CAVEAT, stated because it matters: the is_seed deadlock was broken by flipping ONE already-funded fixture to is_seed=false and fast-forwarding payout_scheduled_at, then restoring it. That changed DATA, not code — the production .eq('is_seed', false) filter ran unmodified and admitted the row on its own merits. So the CODE is proven; a job created non-seed through the real UI is still inferred from the column default, not driven. LIVE-MODE BLOCKER found in the same run: the platform account runs payouts schedule={interval:'daily',delay_days:2}, so two days after a charge its funds are swept to the bank and the charge can no longer fund a transfer (available $0.00). Any payout delayed >2 days past its charge fails balance_insufficient — retries, dispute holds, late Connect onboarding, the stale payout_pending pile. Owner action: set the schedule to manual.

Row after: subscription_tier=pro, subscription_expires_at=2026-10-04T15:55:50+00, subscription_billing_cycle=monthly, stripe_subscription_id=sub_1UBzT2Kp2H4b7tECcjtUHAPr, stripe_customer_id=cus_V9xc6v6SnZd69Q. Still is_seed=true only; all non-seed profiles remain subscription_tier NULL. ATTRIBUTION IS UNRESOLVABLE: this function (check-pro-subscription/index.ts:113-121) and stripe-webhook (handlers/checkoutSessionCompleted.ts:140-147) write the IDENTICAL column set through the same _shared/subscriptionLinkage.ts projection, neither stamps subscription_source (NULL on the one tiered row), and stripe_webhook_events carries only (event_id,event_type,processed_at) with no user/target column.
